description: Replaces an uploaded CSV file's rows, or a workbook's content with a new .xlsx sent as multipart/form-data in the file field. It keeps its id, and a CSV is never replaced by a workbook or the other way round. Reports built on it show the new content after their next run or message to the slides agent. An invalid file leaves the current one in place, and a sheet or range the new workbook no longer has fails its datasheets' reads. Only the user who created it may. From an MCP client, send a workbook with createDatasetUpload and this file's id.

body.description: What the tool creates, changes or sends

csv.description: The file's data, as CSV text: a header row naming the columns, then at least one row of data. With `replaceDataset`, it replaces the file's whole content, header included, and the uploaded file must be a CSV file. The header's names become the column names of the datasheets made from the file: a blank one becomes `Column N`, after the column's position, and a repeated one gets a `_2`, `_3` suffix. Values can be separated by commas, semicolons or tabs, detected from the header row. At most 10 MB.

idempotencyKey.description: A unique value, such as a UUID, that makes retrying this call safe. A retry with the same key within 24 hours answers the first call's result instead of running it again. Use a new key for each new call. From 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters.

params.description: The ids of what the tool acts on

id.description: The uploaded file to replace or delete: the `id` returned by `createDataset`. Only the user who uploaded the file can replace or delete it; for anyone else, the request fails with a `404`, as if the file did not exist.

name: replaceDataset
title: Replace an uploaded file
